name: Palmoplantar keratoderma, Nagashima type

criteria.description: Diffuse, non-progressive hyperkeratosis of the palms and soles extending beyond the palmar and plantar surfaces
Transgrediens pattern with hyperkeratosis extending to dorsal aspects of hands and feet
Onset of symptoms in infancy or early childhood
Lack of significant nail dystrophy or abnormalities
Identification of biallelic mutations in SERPINB7 gene

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of diffuse palmoplantar hyperkeratosis with transgrediens pattern and early childhood onset; genetic confirmation supports diagnosis
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily clinical; genetic testing for SERPINB7 mutations can confirm diagnosis

distinguishingFeatures: Progressive course with more severe hyperkeratosis

redFlags: Rapid progression of hyperkeratosis beyond typical distribution
Development of painful constricting bands or pseudoainhum
Signs of secondary infection or ulceration in hyperkeratotic areas
